chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about a person in Ihram who caught a rabbit or a fox. He said: Regarding the rabbit is (a penalty of) a sheep.

key_terms.شَاةٌ: A sheep (used as the unit of valuation for the penalty)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for killing a rabbit while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the financial expiation (fidyah) for killing a rabbit while in Ihram is established as the value of one sheep, reflecting the proportional valuation system used in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling is derived from the broader Quranic principle of compensating for specific game, illustrating how the Imams clarified the practical application of divine law regarding the sanctity of the sacred precincts.
